title_en: Deeds like ashes on a stormy day
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. A parable or similitude is not a dated event and is not placed in any order: the chapter states only what the ayat present as a similitude, what it is likened to, and what the ayat themselves say. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

chapters.title_en: Deeds like ashes on a stormy day

claims.statement_en: The ayah says that the similitude of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes that the wind blows hard on a stormy day.
They have no power over anything of what they earned.
That, the ayah says, is the far error.

chapters.summary_md: The ayah likens the deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord to ashes that the wind blows hard on a stormy day [c1]. They have no power over anything of what they earned [c2].
chapters.body_md: The ayah says that the similitude of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes [c1]. The wind blows hard on the ashes on a stormy day [c1]. They have no power over anything of what they earned [c2]. That, the ayah says, is the far error [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah gives the similitude in one sentence and then states what follows about those it describes: they have no power over what they earned, and this is the far error [c1][c2][c3]. The picture is of ashes, which are light, and of a wind that blows hard [c1].
chapters.kids_md: The ayah says that the deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord are like ashes [c1]. On a stormy day the wind blows hard on them [c1]. They have no power over anything of what they earned [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the picture shows deeds that cannot be gathered back once the wind has taken them [c1][c2]. Another reading is that the ayah calls this the far error [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which deeds are meant, or who in particular is meant by those who disbelieve in their Lord; no person is named.
- Not established: how the ayah relates to the other ayat on deeds that are lost; this draft cites only 14:18.
- The ayah itself uses the word for a similitude (mathal).
- The words ashtaddat bihi al-rih (the wind blew hard on it) and al-dalal al-baid (the far error) are rendered here in plain words; a scholar may prefer other wording.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: none identified; a scholar should say whether any should be linked to this ayah.
The wording of the far error and of the wind blowing hard is for a scholar to confirm.
